newsitem.title: USA: US West reaffirms commitment to triple-B rating.
newsitem.headline: US West reaffirms commitment to triple-B rating.

text.p: A U.S. West Media Group spokesman reaffirmed the company's commitment to maintaining a "solid" triple-B credit rating in light of the company's ongoing discussions to restructure its partnership with Time-Warner Inc.

"To the extent a restructuring (of the Time Warner partnership) involves taking additional cable subscribers, we would not take on any level of debt that would jeopardize our triple-B credit rating," the spokesman said during a conference call with reporters on Thursday morning, which followed a similar call with Wall Street analysts.
Richard Post, chief financial officer of U.S. West Media, said the company plans to finance the full upgrade of its cable system while maintaining its triple-B rating as well.
A spokesman said the upgrade, which is expected to be completed by the end of 1999, will involve converting the bulk of its current cable system into a broadband communications network.
The network will be able to transmit many more channels as well as provide two-way telephony and internet-access services, he said.
Post said U.S. West is planning a total of $1.2 billion to $1.3 billion of capital expenditures for its domestic cable business in 1997.
Approximately $500 million of that amount would be raised by selling its stake in Teleport Communications Group Inc, a company which provides long-distance telephone services to business customers.

Another $300 million to $500 million would be raised by selling three telephone directory businesses located in the United Kingdom, Poland and Brazil as well as "non-strategic international assets", a spokesman said.
"Non-traditional assets would be those in which we own a small percentage of a company and probably don't have sufficient operating control to make a different in how it's run," he explained.
The remainder of the capital expenditures would be raised from short-term borrowing, Post said.
